data.summary: The "bat" directory is a single scenario definition inside an aio-config/docker-fragment generation system, describing how to install the `bat` syntax-highlighting CLI via the mise version manager. It pairs a declarative `scenario.toml` metadata file with a `fragment.Dockerfile` that performs the idempotent install and verification steps, so the directory is pure infrastructure/config rather than business logic.

file_insights.name: fragment.Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Docker build fragment that installs `bat` at a pinned version through `mise use -g` and verifies the binary is resolvable in both login and non-login shells.
file_insights.source_summary: Contains a comment block explaining that the binary is installed under its canonical name `bat` (no Debian batcat renaming) and resides in /opt/mise/installs. The executable portion is `ARG BAT_VERSION={{version}}` followed by a single chained `RUN` that runs `mise use -g "bat@${BAT_VERSION}"`, `mise ls bat`, and two `command -v bat` guards emitting MISSING(login)/MISSING(non-login) errors and exiting non-zero.
file_insights.detailed_description: This fragment is an L2 "shell layer" piece of a composable Docker image build, run by the aio-config generator. It declares an ARG BAT_VERSION templated from the scenario's version list, then calls `mise use -g` to merge `bat@${BAT_VERSION}` into the global mise config (read-modify-write semantics, so ordering with other mise fragments is idempotent). It finishes with sanity checks (`mise ls bat`, `command -v bat`) under both login and non-login bash to catch PATH/installation failures at build time.
responsibilities: Declare a templated BAT_VERSION build argument
Install/register bat in the global mise tool config
Assert the bat binary is on PATH in login and non-login shells

interfaces.name: RUN (mise use -g bat@${BAT_VERSION} && mise ls bat && command -v bat checks)

file_insights.name: scenario.toml
file_insights.summary: Declarative scenario metadata consumed by `aio-config gen` to resolve which fragment to apply and which version of bat to install.
file_insights.source_summary: A short TOML document with comment headers explaining that it holds scenario metadata while the adjacent fragment.Dockerfile holds install steps. Fields: id = "bat", name = "bat", description describing a syntax-highlighted cat replacement with Git integration installed via the mise aqua backend into /opt/mise/installs, category = "shell", installer = "mise", and one [[versions]] entry labeling version 0.26.1.
file_insights.detailed_description: This TOML file is the entry contract for the bat scenario in the aio-config fragment resolver. It declares the scenario id/name, a human-readable description, the `shell` category, the `mise` installer backend, and a `[[versions]]` table pinning bat to 0.26.1. The generator reads it alongside `fragment.Dockerfile` to template the {{version}} placeholder and emit the correct Docker layer.
responsibilities: Identify the scenario to the fragment resolver
Classify the scenario (shell category, mise installer)
Pin the installable version(s) of bat
